title: Self-Critique and Refinement for Faithful Natural Language Explanations
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
status: Official ACL proceedings metadata verified; paper full text not retrieved
access_depth: Official abstract + author repository README (not full text)
contribution: SR-NLE iteratively critiques and refines post-hoc natural-language explanations, including feedback derived from feature attribution; no additional training is required in the reported method.
limitations: Only official abstract and author README inspected. Self-feedback is not independent ground truth. Exact tested attribution-feedback procedures, intervention assumptions and reported results need full-text scrutiny; no audience-preservation protocol established by these inspected sources.
relevance: Direct prior art against claiming iterative explanation verification/refinement or attribution-guided correction as novel.
baseline_use: Strong candidate baseline for attribution-feedback refinement; source pipeline includes answer, explanation, feedback and refinement runners.

title: Cross-Refine: Improving Natural Language Explanation Generation by Learning in Tandem
venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics
status: Official ACL proceedings metadata verified; paper full text not retrieved
access_depth: Official abstract + author repository README (not full text)
contribution: Uses two LLM roles, generator and critic, to assess, give feedback/suggested explanation and refine an initial NLE without supervised training.
limitations: Abstract/README access only. LLM critique and human preference do not certify target-model faithfulness. Exact evaluation constructs and leakage controls require full text.
relevance: Direct prior art against novelty of a separate explanation critic or two-model generation-and-checking architecture.
baseline_use: Candidate explanation-refinement baseline; compare fairly against its Self-Refine comparator and control call budget.

title: Multi-Level Explanations for Generative Language Models
venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
status: Official ACL proceedings metadata verified; paper full text not retrieved
access_depth: Official abstract + author repository README (not full text)
contribution: MExGen extends perturbation-based attribution such as LIME/SHAP to costly, long-context text generation; scores context parts for influence on outputs and reports automated plus human evaluation.
limitations: Official abstract/README only. Context attribution is not proof of internal causal reasoning and is not itself audience-adapted claim validation. Method targets context-grounded generation rather than the same bounded classification task by default.
relevance: Prior art for model-grounded explanations of LLM outputs and reusable in-context XAI tooling; the application or extending SHAP to text generation alone cannot be new.
baseline_use: Relevant evidence-extraction comparator or reusable toolkit; ICX360 includes MExGen, CELL contrastive prompts and token highlighter. README states Apache2.0, not independently licence-audited here.

title: Faithful Serum: Mitigating the Faithfulness Gap in Textual Explanations of LLM Decisions via Attribution Guidance
venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
status: Official ACL proceedings metadata verified; paper full text not retrieved
access_depth: Official abstract + author repository README (not full text)
contribution: Faithful Serum evaluates omitted influential hints using counterfactuals and guides explanations using PE-LRP token-attribution heatmaps injected at attention level; training-free.
limitations: Official abstract/README only, not full-text verification. Guidance requires open-model internals; author README notes a narrow intervention-strength range and instability/repetition when too high. Its strong claim of actual-evidence faithfulness must be interpreted within its tests.
relevance: Very close 2026 prior art for attribution-grounded explanation generation and intervention-based checks; prevents first-ever grounding-plus-verification claim.
baseline_use: High-priority nearest-method comparator if model/access compatible; otherwise explicit related-work comparison and possibly a reproduced simpler condition.

title: FaithLM: Towards Faithful Explanations for Large Language Models
venue: Proceedings of the 19th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
status: Official ACL proceedings metadata verified; paper full text not retrieved
access_depth: Official abstract + author repository README (not full text)
contribution: FaithLM formalizes explanation faithfulness via prediction shifts when explanation content is contradicted; uses contrary-hint scoring and iteratively refines elicitation prompts and explanations.
limitations: Official abstract plus minimal official README only. Theoretical soundness is an author claim in the abstract, not independently checked. Different intervention semantics from standard input deletion or counterfactual reclassification; cannot treat scores as equivalent.
relevance: Direct 2026 prior art for model-agnostic behavioral explanation assessment linked to iterative improvement.
baseline_use: High-priority behavioral verification comparator; full text needed before implementing its contrary-hint score.

title: Accountable AI with Grounded, Faithful, Consistent, Actionable Rationales: A Case Study in Clinical Trial Matching with VERDICT
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
status: Official ACL proceedings metadata verified; paper full text not retrieved
access_depth: Official abstract + author repository README (not full text)
contribution: VERDICT converts constraints/policies into SMT/MaxSMT and derives eligibility decisions from a solver, exposing assumptions and pivotal conditions that would change outcomes; combines accountable rationale artifacts with a working clinical trial application.
limitations: Official abstract and extensive author README only. Solver-based decisions differ from explanations of an unchanged LLM classifier. Clinical resources and data licensing impose scope costs. README-reported benchmark numbers have not been reproduced; no clinical deployment endorsement.
relevance: Strong prior art for evidence-grounded decision support, audit trails, pivotal/counterfactual conditions and explicit undecided states. Changing the thesis to solver decisions would change Review1 scope.
baseline_use: Architecture/limitation comparator, not automatically a fair same-task numerical baseline. Abstract metadata lists EMNLP2026; collection ingested 2026-10-21 and month October.
